stages.name: Ideation intake
stages.description: Capture the idea, sponsor context, and reason to explore it.
requirements: State the idea without treating an untested solution as an approved requirement.

stages.name: Problem framing
stages.description: Define the user or business problem and the affected population.
requirements: Identify the target user, current problem, and material business context.

stages.name: Stakeholder context
stages.description: Identify accountable stakeholders, users, and material dependencies.
requirements: Record stakeholders whose decisions or operating responsibilities affect delivery.

stages.name: Business architecture alignment
stages.description: Align the proposed change to business capabilities and target operating boundaries.
requirements: Identify affected business capabilities and material operating-model implications.

stages.name: Hypothesis definition
stages.description: State the testable belief that motivates the delivery effort.
requirements: Express a falsifiable relationship between the proposed change and expected outcome.

stages.name: Success measures
stages.description: Define observable measures used to judge the result.
requirements: Define at least one observable success criterion and its evaluation method.

stages.name: Scope definition
stages.description: Set explicit in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries.
requirements: Record both included behavior and deliberate exclusions.

stages.name: Requirements clarification
stages.description: Resolve material product decisions through focused conversation or document input.
requirements: Clarify product behavior, business rules, scenarios, and edge cases at the required depth.

stages.name: Requirements analysis
stages.description: Turn clarified intent into coherent, traceable functional and quality requirements.
requirements: Identify contradictions, dependencies, quality attributes, and missing decisions.

stages.name: Acceptance criteria definition
stages.description: Define testable conditions for the approved behavior.
requirements: Make acceptance criteria observable, unambiguous, and traceable to requirements.

stages.name: Data and integration boundaries
stages.description: Define data classification, persistence, interfaces, and external-system boundaries.
requirements: Record data sources, retention, sensitive-data handling, integrations, and explicit non-integrations.

stages.name: Risk classification
stages.description: Classify delivery risk and identify policy triggers.
requirements: Record risk level and all known governance, security, data, and operational triggers.

stages.name: Requirements approval
stages.description: Present and approve the complete functional build contract.
requirements: Obtain explicit approval of a complete, reviewed, and content-bound Requirements document.

stages.name: Work-item planning
stages.description: Create or validate traceable delivery work items and external references.
requirements: Maintain traceability between requirements, delivery work, and test-management references when integrations apply.

stages.name: Solution design
stages.description: Define the smallest suitable technical design and its material trade-offs.
requirements: Document boundaries, dependencies, data flow, key decisions, and reversibility.

stages.name: UX design
stages.description: Define applicable interaction, visual, accessibility, and responsive behavior.
requirements: Apply enterprise UX standards and specify relevant interaction states.

stages.name: Test strategy
stages.description: Define proportionate verification levels, environments, and evidence.
requirements: Map acceptance and risk to planned automated, manual, security, and non-functional verification.

stages.name: Delivery planning
stages.description: Plan sequencing, dependencies, ownership, and delivery controls.
requirements: Identify dependencies, role assignments, and constraints that affect execution.

stages.name: Build readiness
stages.description: Verify that the approved contract, applicable controls, design, and test plan are ready for implementation.
requirements: Block build when requirements, mandatory controls, design, or verification preparation is incomplete.

stages.name: Implementation
stages.description: Implement the approved scope and applicable standards.
requirements: Build only approved behavior and route material deviations through the controlled requirements process.

stages.name: Developer verification
stages.description: Run proportionate developer-owned checks and capture technical evidence.
requirements: Verify core behavior and technical quality before independent acceptance verification.

stages.name: Security verification
stages.description: Verify triggered security controls and document findings or exceptions.
requirements: Run the security checks required by risk, data, technology, and governance context.

stages.name: Test-case preparation
stages.description: Prepare traceable test cases and test-management records.
requirements: Trace planned test cases to acceptance criteria and applicable risk controls.

stages.name: Test execution
stages.description: Execute the approved verification scope and capture reproducible evidence.
requirements: Record results, failures, deviations, and evidence for the planned verification scope.

stages.name: Acceptance verification
stages.description: Determine whether implemented behavior satisfies the approved acceptance criteria.
requirements: Resolve material failures and obtain the required QA or Product acceptance decision.

stages.name: Release readiness
stages.description: Evaluate operational, governance, change, and deployment controls before release.
requirements: Satisfy applicable tollgates, evidence requirements, rollback preparation, and separation-of-duty controls.

stages.name: Deployment
stages.description: Deploy an approved release through the authorized delivery mechanism.
requirements: Use the approved deployment path and retain deployment and rollback evidence.

stages.name: Production validation
stages.description: Validate the deployed change and operational signals in the target environment.
requirements: Confirm critical behavior, monitoring, and rollback criteria after deployment.

stages.name: Outcome review and disposition
stages.description: Compare results with success measures and decide whether to park, advance, or otherwise disposition the delivery.
requirements: Record the outcome, supporting evidence, rationale, and accountable follow-up.
